output.methodChoice: Collected X3 (yield by scholarship tier) and X6 (yield by admission round). Stopped at two items.
output.brief: The Fall 2026 drop is most likely driven by the revised merit scholarship schedule, not by the Admissions Office or the portal. Applications, admits and admitted GPA all rose. The enrolment fall is concentrated in the Dean's and Merit tiers, where awards were cut (yield fell about 13 points). Presidential awards, unchanged, held steady, and the no-merit tier barely moved. Early-action yield also fell, though its decisions went out on the normal timetable and were not affected by the portal, which argues against the portal as the main cause. The portal and merit-reader staffing delays probably cost some regular-decision students, but are a smaller factor. I'm moderately confident (about 65–75%); the tier comparison is not a randomised test, and the reasons for the yield drop among admits have not been surveyed directly. Next: take the award schedule back to the finance committee with net revenue modelled before next cycle's award letters go out. Set a regular-decision turnaround target. Do not replace the director on this evidence. Hold off on vendor remediation until the missing-document reports are verified.
